title: The Period of Insurance Under the Travel Protection Plans
content:
Cancellation cover under the Travel Protection Plans runs from the moment the certificate is issued, and
every other benefit runs from the moment the insured journey begins until the moment it ends.

## When the journey begins and ends

A journey begins when the traveller leaves their home address for the first booked departure and ends when they
return to it, so cover is not tied to the booked flight times alone. Cover expires at the end of the last day of
the journey and is never extended for convenience.

## Extension and multi-trip cover

1. Where the return is delayed by an event the policy covers, cover extends automatically for the days of the
   delay at no further premium, up to the plan's maximum journey length.
2. A multi-trip plan covers each journey separately up to the plan's maximum length; a journey that runs longer
   is covered for the plan's maximum and not beyond.

## What is excluded and what is covered only by plan

War and civil unrest are excluded on every plan of the Travel Protection Plans. An epidemic or a terrorist
incident is covered only on a plan that says so.

## Points of judgement

| The situation | The answer |
|---|---|
| The traveller is at home and the trip is called off two days before departure | The journey has not begun, and only cancellation cover answers, which has run since the certificate was issued |
| The traveller leaves home at five in the morning for a nine o'clock departure and is hurt in the taxi | The journey has begun, because it begins on leaving the home address, and the benefits that run from inception answer |
| A covered event delays the return by four days on a plan whose maximum journey length is 30 days, the journey having run 27 | Cover extends for three of those days at no further premium, reaching the plan's maximum, and not beyond it |
| The traveller decides at the airport to stay two extra days | Cover expires at the end of the last day of the journey; convenience does not extend it |
